column4: Giving wealth, keeping a covenant, and patience حِينَ ٱلْبَأْسِ culminate in أُولَٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُوا۟; the ayah directly makes truth the completion of costly action, as the section's sound charge does.

أَفَرَءَيْتَ ٱلَّذِى تَوَلَّىٰ introduces a man whose turning away is immediately specified by 53:34 as giving a little and stopping, nearly an exact nonmilitary enactment of the section's aborted charge.
وَأَعْطَىٰ قَلِيلًۭا وَأَكْدَىٰ joins the section's giving verb to an action cut short; 53:33 supplies the man's prior تَوَلَّىٰ, so the pair makes incomplete giving itself a retreat.

When fighting has been mentioned in 47:20 and the matter becomes resolved, فَلَوْ صَدَقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ would mean carrying obedience through; this is the section's claim that truth appears at the point of committed action.
Striving with wealth and lives is the evidence for أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصَّٰدِقُونَ; the ayah explicitly identifies truth with enacted expenditure and struggle.
The pledge لَنَصَّدَّقَنَّ promises that a divine gift will be answered by giving; 9:76-77 show that refusing to complete it turns the promised charity into a lie.
After God gives them bounty, بَخِلُوا۟ بِهِۦ وَتَوَلَّوا۟; stinginess and turning away fuse the section's ungiving man with its retreating fighter.
The broken promise of 9:75-76 ends بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْذِبُونَ, defining lying as failure to carry a pledged act through rather than as words alone.
Spending and fighting before the conquest stand together, and وَكُلًّۭا وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ; this is the section's explicit junction of giving, completed combat, and the fair outcome.
The commanded challenge إِلَّآ إِحْدَى ٱلْحُسْنَيَيْنِ names the section's two fair battlefield outcomes, victory or martyrdom, as all believers await for themselves.
The fighter may be killed or prevail, فَيُقْتَلْ أَوْ يَغْلِبْ, and receives immense reward in either case; it spells out the two good ends compressed into ٱلْحُسْنَيَيْنِ.
Believers spend both property and life, fight, kill and are killed, under a true promise whose fulfillment none exceeds; the ayah unites giving, full combat, martyrdom, and completed truth.
Men who صَدَقُوا۟ مَا عَٰهَدُوا۟ include one who has fulfilled his vow and one still waiting without changing; truth is steadfast completion inside battle exactly as the section describes.
At the sight of the confederates the believers say وَصَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ and increase in submission; 33:23 then shows that affirmed truth embodied in their own kept covenant.
لِّيَجْزِىَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ بِصِدْقِهِمْ states the outcome of the battlefield fidelity in 33:22-23, completing the link between a sound charge and its reward.

God had صَدَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ while they struck the enemy, until courage failed, dispute arose, and they disobeyed; the ayah places fulfilled truth and an interrupted attack on opposite sides of one battle.
Male and female are made reciprocal, then exile, injury, fighting, and death receive promised gardens; this ayah brings the section's sex pair directly into its battlefield and martyrdom outcome.
God loves those who fight in a rank كَأَنَّهُم بُنْيَٰنٌۭ مَّرْصُوصٌۭ; the compact, solid line is the Quranic scene closest to the section's hard metal and sound, sustained assault.
لِمَ تَقُولُونَ مَا لَا تَفْعَلُونَ rebukes the split between assertion and action; 61:4 supplies the battle line in which words must become steadfast deed.
The divine abhorrence of saying what one does not do sharpens the section's distinction between verbal assent and carrying the act through; 61:4 immediately stages the positive form in battle.

At encounter, the command proceeds from striking necks حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَآ أَثْخَنتُمُوهُمْ to binding captives and until war lays down its burdens; it stages a cutting weapon and an assault carried to its defined end.
Iron is sent down فِيهِ بَأْسٌۭ شَدِيدٌۭ; its severe martial force is the most direct Quranic counterpart to the section's hard iron made into an effective weapon.

The governor's wife gives each woman a knife and they cut their hands; the ayah concretely combines a blade handed to another person with the cutting action that distinguishes the section's effective sword.

Game within reach of أَيْدِيكُمْ وَرِمَاحُكُمْ places the spear in an actual striking scene, giving a Quranic object for the dictionary's رُمْحٌ صِدْقٌ, though the context is a test during pilgrimage rather than war.
Those for whom ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ has preceded are عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُونَ from Hell; fair outcome and being kept away from fire converge just as ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ and سَيُجَنَّبُهَا do in the source image.
The revealed warning ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ repeats the source sequence exactly: denial followed by turning away leads to punishment.
At the moment of meeting an advancing enemy, فَلَا تُوَلُّوهُمُ ٱلْأَدْبَارَ expressly forbids the battlefield back-turning heard in the section's وَلَّىٰ هَارِبًا.
Whoever يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍۢ دُبُرَهُ without a tactical exception incurs wrath and Hell; it supplies the destination of the retreat forbidden in 8:15 and mirrored by the source fire.
The laggards will be summoned against أُو۟لِى بَأْسٍۢ شَدِيدٍۢ and must fight or face surrender; وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوْا۟ threatens the renewed retreat that the section opposes to a completed charge.
The besieged had covenanted لَا يُوَلُّونَ ٱلْأَدْبَٰرَ; not turning backs is explicitly a promise to be fulfilled under attack, joining the section's truth and retreat roots.
Flight from death or killing will not benefit the besieged; it states the futility of the battlefield escape whose broken covenant is named in 33:15.

Those who asked for a king so they could fight then تَوَلَّوْا۟ إِلَّا قَلِيلًۭا when fighting was prescribed; intention collapses before execution in the section's precise sense of an aborted charge.
Moses orders his people to enter and وَلَا تَرْتَدُّوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَدْبَارِكُمْ; the warning makes back-turning the act that converts a commanded advance into loss.
فَٱذْهَبْ أَنتَ وَرَبُّكَ فَقَٰتِلَآ إِنَّا هَٰهُنَا قَٰعِدُونَ is the blunt reversal of a sound charge: the addressees leave fighting to others and announce that they will sit.
Satan first guarantees victory, but when the two forces appear نَكَصَ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيْهِ; assurance turns into a literal retreat at contact, embodying the section's charge that fails midway.
At Uhud the believers climb away, heed no one, and leave the Messenger calling from behind; the ayah makes battlefield flight visible after the failure described in 3:152.
Those who تَوَلَّوْا۟ on the day the armies met were made to slip through some of what they had earned; the root names an actual battlefield withdrawal.
Called to fight or at least defend, the hypocrites excuse themselves and say with their mouths what is not in their hearts; the war setting exposes untrue speech through refusal to act.
Those who sat back claim their slain brothers would have lived had they obeyed; إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ challenges them to repel death themselves, turning claimed truth against battlefield avoidance.
The hypocrites promise support, yet if their allies are fought they will not help, and if they do help لَيُوَلُّنَّ ٱلْأَدْبَٰرَ; false assurance ends in the section's back-turning.
Had the disbelievers fought, لَوَلَّوُا۟ ٱلْأَدْبَٰرَ; the root is staged as battlefield rout, the direct opposite of carrying an assault through.
سَيُهْزَمُ ٱلْجَمْعُ وَيُوَلُّونَ ٱلدُّبُرَ predicts a host routed and turning its back, a compact counterpart to the section's flight scene.
At Hunayn numerical confidence failed and ثُمَّ وَلَّيْتُم مُّدْبِرِينَ; the ayah shows a strong-looking force reversing direction under pressure.
The blazing fire تَدْعُوا۟ مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ; it directly joins turning away with the fire that awaits the denier in the source, while 70:15 identifies that fire.
وَلَٰكِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ repeats the source's two verbs in the same order, making denial issue in bodily departure.
أَرَءَيْتَ إِن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ repeats the same denial-and-turning pair while the surrounding scene concerns a man obstructing prayer.
وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا ٱلْأَشْقَى reverses the source relation: the wretched one avoids the reminder, whereas in the source the most Godfearing is made to avoid the fire; 87:12 gives the consequence.
The wretched person who avoids the reminder in 87:11 يَصْلَى ٱلنَّارَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ; avoiding the warning leads into fire, opposite the pious person's being kept from it.
ثُمَّ نُنَجِّى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوا۟ states that the Godfearing are rescued while wrongdoers remain kneeling in Hell, directly matching the shield-like protection of the source's ٱلْأَتْقَى.
God rescues those who feared Him and لَا يَمَسُّهُمُ ٱلسُّوٓءُ; this gives the theological reality represented by the section's shield beside the protected person.
وَأَلَنَّا لَهُ ٱلْحَدِيدَ makes iron pliant for David, a precise reversal of the dictionary's hardest male iron; 34:11 shows that softness enables protective armor rather than ineffective action.

David is commanded to make full coats of mail and measure their links; the softened iron of 34:10 becomes effective protection, setting a boundary on the section's equation of soft metal with weak work.
God teaches David the craft of armor لِتُحْصِنَكُم مِّنۢ بَأْسِكُمْ; it supplies the Quranic protective weapon for the section's shield kept at a fighter's side.
وَسَرَٰبِيلَ تَقِيكُم بَأْسَكُمْ names garments that protect people from their own violence, directly matching the shield's protective function in battle.
The paired men and women include ٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ وَٱلصَّٰدِقَٰتِ and ٱلْمُتَصَدِّقِينَ وَٱلْمُتَصَدِّقَٰتِ; sex, truth, and giving meet without making female action weaker.
ٱلْمُصَّدِّقِينَ وَٱلْمُصَّدِّقَٰتِ pairs charitable men and women under one multiplied reward, joining the sex pair to the giving branch of the same صدق root.
Striving with wealth and selves makes belief into expenditure and struggle; 61:12-13 then divide its beloved result into the next-world reward and near victory.
Forgiveness and gardens are the enduring outcome of the striving in 61:11; paired with the worldly victory of 61:13, they illuminate the section's two fair outcomes.
نَصْرٌۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَفَتْحٌۭ قَرِيبٌۭ is the other desired good beside 61:12's gardens, giving victory as the present-world partner of promised reward.
When believers meet a force, فَٱثْبُتُوا۟ commands them to stand firm; it is the positive battlefield act opposed to breaking off a charge.
Dispute would make believers fail and lose their force, so they must be patient; the ayah identifies the internal fracture that turns a firm line into a failed assault.
Those fighting with prophets neither lost heart, weakened, nor yielded; the triple negation gives the sustained combat denoted by the section's صدق branch.
وَلَا تَهِنُوا۟ فِى ٱبْتِغَآءِ ٱلْقَوْمِ forbids weakening in pursuit despite shared pain, making perseverance the distinguishing feature of the attack.
فَلَا تَهِنُوا۟ وَتَدْعُوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱلسَّلْمِ forbids losing resolve while believers have the upper hand, closely matching the section's charge that must not be abandoned.
The Prophet must urge believers to fight, and twenty patient fighters may overcome two hundred; patience supplies the human firmness behind the section's solid weapon.
God acknowledges فِيكُمْ ضَعْفًۭا and reduces the ratio while still requiring patient resistance; the ayah distinguishes real weakness from simply abandoning combat.

After the river test, some say they have no power against Goliath, while those expecting to meet God answer that a small steadfast force can defeat a large one; one army divides into faltering and sustained resolve.
Facing Goliath, the faithful ask for poured-out patience and firm feet before seeking victory; the prayer articulates what lets the charge reach its end.
They defeat the enemy by God's permission and David kills Goliath; it supplies the completed victory sought in 2:250 and contrasts the collapse voiced in 2:249.
Two Godfearing men command ٱدْخُلُوا۟ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْبَابَ and promise victory once the entry is made; it is the advance the larger people refuse in 5:24.
The command to go forth light or heavy and strive with wealth and lives fuses material giving with refusal to let difficulty halt the campaign.
Those deterred by distance swear they would have marched if able, but God knows إِنَّهُمْ لَكَٰذِبُونَ; campaign refusal gives their lie its enacted meaning.
Had they intended to go out they would have prepared, but they were held back and told to sit; lack of preparation exposes a professed campaign as an action never carried through.
The ones left behind rejoice in sitting and dislike striving with wealth and lives; their settled refusal reverses the section's giver who completes the attack.
Because they accepted sitting the first time, the laggards are told they will never again go out or fight with the Prophet; initial withdrawal becomes exclusion from the completed campaign.
The Messenger and believers strive with wealth and lives and receive ٱلْخَيْرَٰتُ; their enacted giving and combat form the positive counterpart to the sitters of the passage.
Those killed in God's path are alive and provided for with their Lord; the ayah explains why martyrdom can be one of the section's two fair battlefield outcomes.
Those killed in God's path must not be called dead; the correction supplies the life beyond death assumed when martyrdom is named a good outcome.
لَقَدْ صَدَقَ ٱللَّهُ رَسُولَهُ ٱلرُّءْيَا بِٱلْحَقِّ is realized in secure entry and a near conquest; truth is shown becoming historical action and victory.
بَأْسُهُم بَيْنَهُمْ شَدِيدٌۭ sounds like severe force, yet their hearts are divided; the ayah warns that outward hardness without inward cohesion is not the section's sound charge.
The ayah distinguishes uninjured sitters from those striving with wealth and lives and gives the latter higher rank; it makes enacted commitment, rather than a claim to belief, the boundary.
When fighting is prescribed, a group fears people as God should be feared and asks for delay; the verse stages resolve collapsing precisely when combat becomes obligatory.
Two groups nearly lose courage even though God is their protector; the near-failure marks the threshold between a charge sustained by trust and one abandoned.
The question أَفَإِي۟ن مَّاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ ٱنقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَعْقَٰبِكُمْ makes turning on one's heels after the leader's loss the reversal of faithful persistence.
During the siege some claim their houses are exposed, though God says they only intend flight; a spoken excuse masks the bodily retreat that the image treats as lying in action.
God knows the obstructionists who summon others away and come to battle only a little; partial attendance without committed fighting is the section's interrupted action.
If the confederates return, the fearful wish to be among desert Arabs merely asking for news and would fight only a little; distance and token action expose their failed commitment.
The Bedouin laggards plead that property and family occupied them, saying with tongues what is absent from hearts; campaign absence makes their speech false in action.
Asked to march, believers are reproached for clinging heavily to the earth; bodily heaviness becomes the contrary image to a charge brought fully forward.
The woman who unravels her yarn after it was strong figures covenant-breaking as undoing completed work; it is a nonmilitary counterpart to the attack begun and then abandoned.
أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى ٱلْكُفَّارِ رُحَمَآءُ بَيْنَهُمْ gives firmness and mercy their proper objects; it keeps the section's hard/soft contrast from becoming a claim that hardness is always superior.
Whoever does righteous deeds, male or female, enters the Garden without injustice; the ayah blocks the weapon lexicon's male/strong and female/weak labels from becoming a scale of human efficacy.
مَنْ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنثَىٰ receives good life and reward on the same condition of faith, separating natural sex from the dictionary's grading of iron.
Creation مِن ذَكَرٍۢ وَأُنثَىٰ leads to the criterion إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ; piety, not the section's figurative hard/soft gender names, sets human worth.
Those kept far from Hell in 21:101 do not hear even its faint sound; this describes how complete the shield-like separation from fire is.
قُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَأَهْلِيكُمْ نَارًۭا commands active protection from fire, the moral action rendered visible by the section's shield.
Abraham asks وَٱجْنُبْنِى وَبَنِىَّ أَن نَّعْبُدَ ٱلْأَصْنَامَ; the same causative root means being kept away from danger, clarifying the protective force heard in سَيُجَنَّبُهَا.
Pharaoh فَكَذَّبَ وَعَصَىٰ rejects and disobeys; 79:22 turns that refusal into bodily withdrawal and renewed hostile action.
ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعَىٰ follows denial with turning back and active striving against Moses, paralleling the source sequence while showing that retreat from truth can still be energetic opposition.
The one who تَوَلَّىٰ وَكَفَرَ is singled out for the greatest punishment in 88:24, a close semantic parallel to denial, turning, and fire in the source.
فَيُعَذِّبُهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلْعَذَابَ ٱلْأَكْبَرَ supplies the consequence for the turning unbeliever of 88:23, completing that parallel to the source warning.
ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ وَٱسْتَكْبَرَ makes the rejecter's inward arrogance bodily as a turned back; 74:26 then gives his fire-bound end.
سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ is the destination of the man who turned back in 74:23, repeating the source movement from rejection and withdrawal to fire.
مَقَٰمِعُ مِنْ حَدِيدٍۢ supplies an explicit iron striking weapon, though it belongs to Hell's punishment rather than a human battlefield.
Zulqarnayn uses blocks of iron, heats them, and pours molten copper over them to make a barrier; hard metal here serves construction and defense rather than a cutting assault.
قُلْ كُونُوا۟ حِجَارَةً أَوْ حَدِيدًا invokes iron as the imagined extreme of resistant hardness, supporting the physical quality behind the dictionary's hard iron.
قَابَ قَوْسَيْنِ names the bow as a measure of nearness rather than as a fired weapon; it preserves the section's bow object while showing a different Quranic use.

In danger prayer one company stands while taking its weapons, then another replaces it with precautions and arms; the alternating armed groups echo the section's weapon passed between hands, although no transfer is stated.
Preparing all available force and tethered horses turns readiness into deterrent power; it supplies the organized martial preparation presupposed by a firm charge.
The fighters' prayer وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا asks for firm feet before victory, giving bodily language to the section's refusal to turn and flee.
God promises to support those who support His cause and وَيُثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَكُمْ; firm feet are the bodily opposite of the retreating back.

The Prophet's permission delayed disclosure of those who spoke truth and the liars among campaign excuse-makers; 9:42 supplies the false oath and avoided march that give this test its concrete content.

During the Hour of Hardship some hearts nearly swerved, yet God turned to the Prophet, emigrants, and helpers who followed him; the near-defection and preserved following illuminate a campaign carried through strain.
Being killed or dying in God's path leads to forgiveness and mercy better than accumulated goods; it explains the value assigned to the death side of the section's two fair outcomes.
Those who emigrate and are then killed or die receive رِزْقًا حَسَنًۭا; the good provision makes death in committed service an attained good rather than a failed campaign.

وَأَنَّهُۥ خَلَقَ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ repeats the source's created male/female pair, anchoring the weapon terms in the primary biological sense from which the dictionary metaphor departs.
فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ again grounds the two weapon labels in the Quranic pair of created sexes.
God يَهَبُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ إِنَٰثًۭا and يَهَبُ male children, bringing divine giving and the female/male pair into one ayah without the weapon lexicon's hierarchy.
God may pair offspring ذُكْرَانًۭا وَإِنَٰثًۭا or make one barren; following 42:49, the pairing remains wholly governed by His gift.
